articles.title: MVP SGA Reacts to Thunder Losing, Changing His Game amid Injuries to Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams
articles.summary: Oklahoma State Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is finding a silver lining with injuries to key players presenting a challenge to the team.
articles.body:
Oklahoma State Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is finding a silver lining with injuries to key players presenting a challenge to the team.

"We can't be at the top of the mountain every night for the next decade," he said, per ESPN's Tim MacMahon . "It doesn't work like that. It's motivation for me."

The Thunder have lost six of their last eight. Their slide coincides with Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace all being sidelined for significant stretches.

In the aftermath of the 113-112 defeat to the Los Angeles Clippers on Nov. 13, Gilgeous-Alexander asserted the difficult period is "kind of fun" in a way.

"We've kind of had the wind at our back for the last couple of years, had our way a lot of nights," he said. "Having adversity, it's kind of fun. I embrace it. It will make me better. It will make us better."

The two-time reigning MVP also reflected on how he has had to adapt. He was already a high-volume player, and now he needs to lead the show even more.

"I've always been at the top of the scouting report," Gilgeous-Alexander told MacMahon. "It's only amplified with guys out.

"Then [I'm] having to start games differently just because of the personnel out there. I've got to be more aggressive some nights to start the game. Typically, when we have our full roster, I'll get guys going and ease into the game. Some nights with men down, you can't really do that."

Some drew big-picture conclusions once the scale of the Thunder's injury crisis became clear. The NBA has made it harder to maintain a championship contender across multiple seasons, with OKC trading Luguentz Dort in the summer largely for financial considerations.

The title window hasn't closed, but a lost year is a bigger missed opportunity for the 2024-25 champion.

Maybe the Thunder's present situation will help them discover new things that aid in their quest for success once they're back to full strength.

articles.title: Donte DiVincenzo Injury Update, Latest NBA Rumors Reveal Timeline to Return for T-Wolves Guard
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves announced Tuesday that guard Donte DiVincenzo has been cleared for team activities as he works his way back from a torn Achilles.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves announced Tuesday that guard Donte DiVincenzo has been cleared for team activities as he works his way back from a torn Achilles.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported DiVincenzo is aiming to return around Jan. 1.

Minnesota is third in the Western Conference at 13-5 despite missing DiVincenzo and seeing Anthony Edwards go down with a knee injury in October.

Some questioned whether LaMelo Ball was the right star to target in a blockbuster trade. The move looks pretty shrewd now with how much he has had to anchor the backcourt. Ball is averaging 17.2 points and 5.6 assists.

Paying a premium to retain Ayo Dosunmu was also a sound investment. His 18.2 points per game are third on the team, and he's shooting 44.8 percent from beyond the arc.

Getting DiVincenzo back by early January would be a huge boost for the team.

The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski noted he's way ahead of schedule. Damian Lillard, Tyrese Haliburton, Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson all missed more than a calendar year. DiVincenzo might be suiting up 10 months removed from his Achilles tear.

The Wolves have no vague idea of when Edwards will be playing again, so they could be a ways off from competing at full strength. DiVincenzo's presence will at least alleviate the burden on Ball and Dosunmu a bit.

articles.title: Imparable crecimiento de la Euroliga: estrenará su propia Liga de Verano en 2027
articles.standfirst: Un torneo internacional con seis equipos y vocación de crecimiento. El proyecto refuerza su capacidad para generar iniciativas, abrir mercados y ampliar su influencia en el baloncesto
articles.summary: Un torneo internacional con seis equipos y vocación de crecimiento. El proyecto refuerza su capacidad para generar iniciativas, abrir mercados y ampliar su influencia en el baloncesto
articles.body: La Euroliga sigue ampliando sus horizontes. la máxima competición continental estrenará en 2027 su propia Liga de Verano, un nuevo proyecto con el que pretende crear un punto de encuentro internacional para jugadores, entrenadores y profesionales del baloncesto, según adelantó Eurohoops. Es una iniciativa que vuelve a poner de manifiesto la capacidad de la organización para impulsar nuevos formatos, detectar oportunidades y desarrollar propuestas que van más allá de la competición tradicional. Los planes de crecimiento de la Euroliga no se limitan a la ampliación de su estructura hasta los 24 equipos ni a la incorporación de nuevas franquicias. La organización presidida por su dirección ejecutiva, encabezada por Chus Bueno, trabaja también en la creación de nuevos espacios de desarrollo y negocio que permitan reforzar su posición dentro del panorama internacional del baloncesto. La primera edición de esta Liga de Verano podría contar con seis equipos y se disputaría durante aproximadamente diez días, incluyendo una semana de competición. Su celebración está prevista una vez concluidas las ligas nacionales y antes del tradicional torneo de verano de la NBA en Las Vegas. La ciudad que albergará el estreno todavía no está decidida, aunque se espera que el proyecto completo se presente en la próxima reunión de la Junta Directiva, prevista para el 30 de noviembre. La propuesta nace con una clara vocación internacional. El objetivo es reunir a jugadores y entrenadores procedentes de clubes de la Euroliga y la Eurocup, universidades estadounidenses y programas de baloncesto de África y Asia. Una combinación que permitiría generar nuevas oportunidades para el desarrollo de jugadores, facilitar la captación de talento y favorecer el intercambio de conocimientos entre distintas culturas baloncestísticas. La intención es que el torneo no sea un acontecimiento aislado, sino una plataforma anual que vaya ganando dimensión y relevancia con el paso de las temporadas. La Euroliga quiere comenzar con un formato reducido de seis participantes para después desarrollar progresivamente una competición capaz de hacerse un hueco propio en el calendario internacional. El proyecto supone, además, una nueva muestra de la ambición de una organización que lleva años diversificando sus iniciativas y explorando fórmulas para ampliar su influencia. La creación de competiciones, la expansión de su estructura y la búsqueda de nuevas vías de conexión con otros mercados forman parte de una estrategia que pretende consolidar a la Euroliga como algo más que una competición de clubes. No será la primera experiencia de la organización en este terreno. La Euroliga ya impulsó en el pasado, junto a Verde Sport, la Liga de Verano ULEB en Jesolo (Italia), aunque aquella iniciativa tuvo una duración de una sola temporada. Ahora, con un planteamiento más ambicioso y una clara vocación de continuidad, la Euroliga pretende recuperar aquella idea y convertirla en un proyecto de mayor alcance. El reto será transformar una competición de verano en una herramienta estable para conectar mercados, descubrir talento y generar nuevas oportunidades para el baloncesto europeo. Con este movimiento, la Euroliga vuelve a demostrar que su capacidad de crecimiento no depende únicamente de lo que sucede durante la temporada regular. También pasa por saber crear nuevos productos, gestionar proyectos de alcance internacional y anticiparse a las necesidades de una industria en constante evolución. La Liga de Verano de 2027 será el próximo desafío de una organización que quiere seguir ampliando su protagonismo en el baloncesto mundial.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Reveals WNBA Offseason Bucket List, Golf Goals in Video With Travis, Jason Kelce
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark's offseason away from the WNBA will include a stop at one of the most legendary golf courses in the world.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark's offseason away from the WNBA will include a stop at one of the most legendary golf courses in the world.

The Indiana Fever star said last week on the New Heights podcast she's hopeful of attending Super Bowl LXI in Inglewood, California. She's also aiming to play a round at Augusta National Golf Club, adding she has "a couple of opportunities to do that" (30:30 mark).

Clark has golfed recreationally for most of her life. She said in a 2023 interview with Big Ten Network she started playing in elementary school.

Fans got to see the three-time All-Star in action at the Annika pro-am last fall.

Clark estimated her handicap is around 15, which is pretty solid for a full-time basketball player. She quipped to hosts Travis and Jason Kelce she benefits from starting off all the way up at the forward tees since she can get as much as 230 yards off her drives.

Augusta National has some of the most exclusive membership on the planet, and the course is closed to members for the best golfing months on the calendar.

Pretty much anybody who has picked up a set of clubs has dreamed about stepping onto the first tee at Augusta. Clark is one of the rare few who's presented with the chance.

articles.title: Hayes-Davis aparta del liderato al Valencia Basket con un triplazo sobre la bocina
articles.standfirst: El alero anota desde más de ocho metros para dar el triunfo al Panathinaikos y frustra el gran esfuerzo de los taronjas
articles.summary: El alero anota desde más de ocho metros para dar el triunfo al Panathinaikos y frustra el gran esfuerzo de los taronjas
articles.body: Un triplazo de Hayes-Davis sobre la bocina y desde más de ocho metros acabó con el líder Valencia Basket. Sólo así, con sucesos extraordinarios, cae este equipo. Los taronjas tuvieron al poderoso Panathinaikos a su merced (83-80 a 39 segundos del final), pero le rescataron la aparición de dos de sus estrellas. Primero Nunn, con un triple de siete metros, y luego el verdugo definitivo, con el tiro de gracia, dejaron dos destellos ganadores que apartaron a los valencianos de la primera plaza. Los dos equipos han cambiado mucho con respecto a la temporada pasada. Numerosas caras nuevas, pero la misma intensidad. El duelo de este martes recordó a la serie de playoffs del curso pasado, que también tuvo partidos resueltos sobre la bocina, incluido uno por Hayes-Davis. Fue una de las mejores que se recuerdan en la historia de la Euroliga. Este nuevo enfrentamiento no tuvo nada que envidiar a aquellos. La derrota es dolorosa para el Valencia, pero su consuelo es haber resistido a un transatlántico en un partido jugado a contrapelo en el que sólo en dos buenas rachas pudo imponer el baloncesto que le gusta. El resto del tiempo, el Panathinaikos le cambió el paso y le obligó a bajar al barro. En un gran trabajo defensivo destacaron Saint-Supéry, Cárdenas, Corbalán... Todos ellos se encargaron en algún momento de Nunn, al que contuvieron bien durante la primera mitad. Después, el talento se desbordó. Metió 13 puntos, pero en momentos clave. Shorts lideró un día más a los taronjas. Indefendible por momentos, es todo personalidad y carácter. Acabó con 15 puntos, siete asistencias y tres recuperaciones. Suya fue la canasta del 83-80. No pudo rematar Brooks, que fue de más a menos. Hizo 14 puntos y falló un triple crucial a falta de 10 segundos y con empate a 83. Hayes-Davis, sin embargo, no perdonó. El Valencia pudo ser él mismo en un tramo del primer cuarto para rehacerse de un flojo inicio. Brooks metió ocho puntos seguidos incluidos dos triples y Osetkowski metió otro para concretar un parcial de 11-0. Cárdenas y Corbalán le habían dado otro aire al equipo, pero Grant y la aparición de Yabusele mandaron en el segundo cuarto. El Panathinaikos no necesita ni puntería (1/9 en triples) para irse arriba al descanso: 34-39. Los griegos se fueron nueve arriba tras volver de los vestuarios (36-45). En el momento de mayor apuro se vio la mejor versión del Valencia, una en la que lució una defensa extraordinaria que le permitió volar. Tres minutos de baloncesto total para firmar un parcial de 13-0 con Shorts y Mirotic delante. Detrás mordían todos. Nunn se quitó los grilletes y, ayudado por el rebote ofensivo, el PAO devolvió el golpe con un 0-11 (57-64). En el último cuarto, apariciones de Rogkavopoulos y Juancho mantenían arriba a los visitantes, pero un par de robos del Valencia y el trabajo de Sako voltearon el asunto (75-74). El pívot fue de los destacados (13+7), pero volvió a flojear en el tiro libre (1/6) y arrastró a su equipo (10/19). Con el marcador convertido en un péndulo, Shorts lo puso del lado taronja. Dos de las estrellas de Obradovic acabaron decidiendo. 83.- Valencia Basket (19+15+25+24): TJ Shorts (15), Saint-Supéry (5), Taylor (5), Osetkowski (6), Sako (13) -cinco titular- Cárdenas (7), Moore (2), Corbalán (4), Puerto (-), Brooks (14), Gueye (4) y Mirotic (8). 86.- Panathinaikos (19+20+25+22): Francisco (4), Bonga (2), Hayes-Davis (11), Yabusele (10), Fall (6) -cinco titular- Badio (-), Rogkavapoulos (10), Grant (14), Nunn (13), Lessort (9) y Hernangómez (7). Árbitros: Belosevic (SER), Koljensic (MNE) y Sacys (LTU). Sin eliminados. Incidencias: partido correspondiente a la décimo cuarta jornada de la fase regular de la Euroliga disputado en el Roig Arena ante 14.130 espectadores.

articles.title: Shavon Shields arruina la brega del Barça con siete triples en la segunda parte
articles.standfirst: El excelso alero resucita al Fenerbahce en su momento más bajo (59-47) liderando un parcial de 3-22 (62-69). Las cinco bajas azulgranas lastraron su encomiable resistencia
articles.summary: El excelso alero resucita al Fenerbahce en su momento más bajo (59-47) liderando un parcial de 3-22 (62-69). Las cinco bajas azulgranas lastraron su encomiable resistencia
articles.body: Shavon Shields anotó la primera canasta del Fenerbahce y luego desapareció, como si se le hubiera tragado la tierra. Tras un tobogán de parciales y contraparciales el mermado Barça pareció encarrilar el triunfo (59-47, min 27). Hasta que Shields resurgió como por arte de magia para comandar la remontada turca con 24 puntos más y 7/12 triples que arruinaron el esfuerzo de los azulgranas (77-83). El excelso alero entró en trance y en ocho minutos anotó cinco triples para liderar, con ayuda de Larkin y Juzang, un brutal parcial de 3-22 en apenas ocho minutos con el que el Fenerbahce dio la vuelta al marcador colocándose en una situación inmejorable que no desaprovechó. No se rindió el Barça, que con triples de Umude (69-71) y Martin (77-80) acarició la remontada. Pero Shields, con su séptimo triple y dos tiros libres abortó el conato de sorpasso y Horton-Tucker abrochase el triunfo turco con tres tiros libres y una canasta postrera. Fue la tercera derrota consecutiva de un Barça que reaccionó tras su flojo inicio (8-14) con un 20-7 (28-21, min 10) y un gran Minaya. El Fenerbahce contestó con un 2-13 con arreones de Larkin y Clyburn (30-34). Y Minaya, Martin y Umude llevaron a los azulgranas a su máxima (59-47) antes de la irrupción del ciclón Shields. Las bajas de Punter, Gibson, Nebo, Makoundou y Evbuomwoman pesaron más en el Barça que las de Melli y Key en el Fenerbahce de Jasikevicius, ídolo de un Palau que tuvo que rumiar su dolorosa derrota con Shavon Shields de ejecutor supremo.. 77 - Barça (28+17+16+16): Robinson (12), Brizuela (2), Minaya (13), Parra (4), Nkamhoua (3) -cinco inicial-, Martin (13), Umude (18), Ubal (1), Núñez (5) y Balcerowski (6). 83- Fenerbahce (21+18+14+30): Larkin (19), Shields (26), Clyburn (7), Horton Tucker (11), Powell (2) -cinco inicial-, Bingham (-), Baldwin IV (5), Sanli (3), Juzang (6) y Sariunas (4). Árbitros: Tomislav Hordov, Kristaps Kostantinovs y Luka Kardum. Eliminados: Sanli (min.33) y Powell (min.40). Incidencias: partido de la decimocuarta jornada de la Liga Endesa disputado en el Palau Blaugrana ante 5.698 espectadores.

articles.title: Pistons' Cade Cunningham to miss Tuesday's NBA Cup matchup vs. Magic due to right knee soreness
articles.summary: Cunningham was scratched from the lineup after being listed as probable up until a half-hour before tip-off.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham is out for Tuesday's NBA Cup matchup with the Orlando Magic . He was a late scratch due to right knee soreness after being listed as probable on the injury report until a half-hour before tip-off.

Cunningham, 25, has missed only one game this season for the Pistons, sitting out last week's 122-109 win over the New Orleans Pelicans , also due to right knee soreness. Javonte Green replaced Cunningham in Detroit's starting lineup for that contest, scoring 18 points with seven rebounds.

"He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that," Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff told reporters Tuesday , via MLive's Jacob Richman. "He's going to go out and compete and give us what he's got, but he's fighting through a lot."

Cunningham scored a season-low five points in Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Atlanta Hawks, shooting 2-for-9 in 33 minutes. His 15 assists were his highest total this season, but he also committed six turnovers.

The Pistons have lost two straight games and have a 10-6 record that has them tied for fifth in the Eastern Conference .

In his 15 games this season, Cunningham leads the Pistons in scoring with 24.2 points per game, while averaging 8.3 assists, 5.1 rebounds and 1.3 steals. He's shooting 32% on 92 3-point attempts.

Detroit will also be without Duncan Robinson (left quad strain) and Jalen Duren (strained right hamstring) against the Magic. However, Duren appears to be on his way back after being assigned to the Pistons' G League affiliate for Wednesday's practice.

The Pistons next play on Friday versus the Milwaukee Bucks.

articles.title: 5-Star Guard Jalen Davis Reveals CBB Commitment Decision Between Gonzaga, UNC More
articles.summary: Jalen Davis is staying close to home.
articles.body:
The 5-star guard from Washington announced on Tuesday that he would commit to Gonzaga, giving the Bulldogs the top-ranked recruit in the state.

He chose Gonzaga over North Carolina, UCLA and Washington.

Ranking Top 9 Players to Watch in MCBB 👀

"Coach Few is incredibly competitive and knows the game inside and out," Davis said, per ESPN's Jeff Borzello and Paul Biancardi . "I believe in his vision for me. I want to win and make the right reads. I watch film of Ryan Nembhard and Jalen Suggs because their games are similar to mine."

The 6-foot-4 guard out of Bremerton High School in Washington is ranked as the No. 29 prospect in ESPN's Next 100 and is their sixth-ranked shooting guard.

Davis led the Adidas 3SSB AAU circuit in scoring and steals last summer for the Slow Grind Elite squad, where he averaged 24.3 points and 2.8 steals over 12 games.

North Carolina heavily pursued Davis, but he had long been expected to stay out west. A versatile guard who can be a playmaker as a point guard or create his own offense at the two, the two-time Washington state high school champion made his announcement at his high school on Tuesday afternoon.

"I trusted my gut," Davis told ESPN. "From the moment I visited Gonzaga, it felt like home. The Kennel has a great atmosphere. Those are the people I want to surround myself with, both on and off the court."

Before narrowing down his list, Davis had also considered Stanford, Texas Tech, BYU, Iowa, Ole Miss, TCU and USC.

Davis is Gonzaga's second commit for 2027 along with Dooney Johnson, another top-ranked shooting guard prospect, giving Bulldogs coach Mark Few his first multiple top-30 signings since 2021, according to ESPN, when he signed Chet Holmgren and Hunter Sallis. Davis is the highest-ranked prospect to join the program since that recruiting class.

The Bulldogs are 3-1 and ranked No. 22 in the country so far this season.

articles.title: Thanks to sustained health, Daniel Gafford has been man in middle Mavs have been missing
articles.summary: After an injury-riddled 2025-26, Gafford has been a consistent presence for Dallas so far this season.
articles.body:
DENVER – The NBA Cup is in its fourth year of existence, but the tournament's prize money is one of the primary incentives to compete if you ask Daniel Gafford.

"A lot of guys are coming out and they're playing their tails off because who doesn't want a good stack of cash?" Gafford said after Tuesday's shootaround at Ball Arena. "From a team perspective, we lock in and it's just another game on our schedule. We want to win games. We want to stack these wins."

The Dallas Mavericks entered their pivotal NBA Cup matchup against the Denver Nuggets in the midst of their third three-game win streak of the season, hoping to use the lessons they learned from earlier in the season to extend it to four. Their attention to detail has been a key difference, but they're also getting healthier by the day.

Gafford's sustained health has contributed to those victories. For the Mavericks, that means they have a reliable starter at the center position who has regained his status as one of the most efficient scorers at the rim and shot blockers in the NBA.

The eighth-year big man has played in every game this season, averaging 8.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.6 blocks per game. He ranks eighth in the league in blocks per game, which is a key reason why the Mavericks are 12th in the NBA in defensive rating.

Gafford said he feels good holding down the paint while they await reinforcements from Dereck Lively II, who remains sidelined to rehabilitate from his right foot surgery .

"I'm a junkyard dog, man. I'm from Arkansas," Gafford said. "It ain't really too much that can hold me down."

Last season, Gafford missed 27 games to injury, mainly because of a lingering right ankle sprain. Despite suffering a right shoulder stinger in last Saturday's loss to Cleveland , he's been consistent and has scored in double figures in seven games this season. He's also added the occasional 3-pointer to his arsenal, with a perfect mark from distance on his two attempts.

"When bigs start making them, they change their game," said Mavericks coach Dusty May. "He's changing his game but it's to be an enforcer down low."

When the Mavericks are healthy, they have two big men who could start between Gafford and Lively, who spent a portion of shootaround sprinting, jogging and working on drills that included light jumps.

Gafford's primary backup center has been rookie Morez Johnson Jr., the No. 9 overall pick. Both players go through their pregame routines at the same time, lending itself to a natural partnership. Johnson is averaging 6.3 points and 4.7 rebounds and has connected on a 3-pointer in each of his last two games. The veteran big man said Johnson has developed well despite a slow start due to shin injuries.

"He's asserting himself in his role," Gafford said. "He's rebounding a lot. He's an energy guy. He's one of the strongest guys on our team, too. It's hard for a lot of people to move him. He's going to get into a lot of people's heads when it comes to setting screens and going for rebounds."

As for Gafford, he remains one of the best screen setters on the team and he's third in rebounding behind P.J. Washington and Cooper Flagg.

For the Mavericks to remain above .500, they'll need Gafford to continue to stay healthy and efficient on both sides of the floor.

articles.title: Analysis: No. 19 BYU melts down late in Maui, struggling mightily against elite Ole Miss defense
articles.summary: Leading by 14 points at halftime, the Cougars committed 15 second-half turnovers against five made field goals.
articles.body:
LAHAINA, Hawaii — Less than 24 hours after opening its Maui Invitational stay with a second-half comeback victory, BYU found itself as the team collapsing after halftime.

Having led Ole Miss by 14 after 20 minutes, the Cougars allowed the rabid Rebels to explode for 17 unanswered points out of intermission and never recovered, ultimately falling 73-63 for their first loss of the campaign.

There would have been no shame for BYU in losing to Ole Miss — the best opponent it's faced thus far in the season — and doing so on little rest and with star point guard Rob Wright III sidelined.

But to have led the Rebels by as many as 18 points, only to end up losing by 10? To play their best half of the season and follow it with their worst?

It was a brutal, disheartening outcome for the Cougars, and one that will be tough to flush ahead of Wednesday's final Maui contest.

"Tale of two halves, obviously," Kevin Young told reporters postgame. "We came out of the gate with great intensity, great ball security, great defense. And then, obviously, at the end of the first half and into the second, they obviously took the game over.

"So you've got to give Ole Miss all the credit. They played really good, they clearly accepted whatever coach (Chris) Beard said to them at halftime. We've got to be better, bottom line. In these types of environments, you've got to have a short memory, so we're trying to move on to the next game."

BYU was unfazed early against the vaunted, disruptive Ole Miss defense, scoring 40 points before halftime at an average of 1.2 points per possession. The Cougars appeared confident, comfortable and were seemingly cruising to Wednesday's Maui title game, only for the cruise to sink in spectacular, Titanic fashion.

Ole Miss' 17-0 run out of halftime soon ballooned to a 32-10 stretch. Through the first 15 minutes of the second half, BYU managed just two made field goals, while the Rebels generated turnovers left and right and cashed them in for easy transition buckets.

When Ole Miss turned up the heat in the second half, the Cougars slipped in their own sweat. Much of the guts and grit BYU displayed against Washington on Monday were absent in Tuesday's crunch time.

"We knew they were going to come out (of halftime ready to play). We said in the locker room, 'They're over there, going 'rah rah,' trying to get going,' and we came out and looked like we didn't expect that to happen, but it did," Young said of BYU's second-half struggles.

"I think it was a tough learning moment for us as a team, in getting a lead, keeping a lead and setting the tone in the second half."

In the final 20 minutes, BYU shot just 5 of 20 (25%) from the field and coughed up 15 turnovers, including five from Bruce Branch III alone.

If not for 17 free-throw attempts (10 coming from Collin Chandler), BYU would have barely had any sort of second-half offense. The Cougars were in constant distress, as evidenced by their turnover tally being three times that of their made field goals.

"In the first half we made it easy because we were the ones that came out and set the tone, we were getting turnovers and getting out in transition," Chandler said.

"They're a great set defense team, and they force turnovers that way. I think they're the best in the country at doing that ... We're a very experienced team, but that was a little bit of an inexperienced look for us, thinking they weren't going to come out and do that in second half. They completely flipped the script."

Chandler was sensational for the Cougars, pouring in a career-high 34 points on 9 of 18 shooting while adding eight rebounds and a pair of steals. The junior guard also went 12 of 13 from the foul line, which proved to be BYU's only source of consistent offense after halftime, as previously mentioned.

"We're in a little bit of a tough spot without Rob Wright, honestly, so that puts a little bit more responsibility on me to get downhill," Chandler said. "I think I learned a lot today. There's a lot that I can grow from in mistakes that I made, and so today was a good opportunity for me to learn especially and move on to tomorrow and get better at those things that Ole Miss exposed."

Unfortunately for Chandler, his 34 points were joined by just 29 from the rest of his teammates, who were stripped for 19 turnovers as well.

Aside from Chandler's three made triples, BYU netted just a single 3-pointer in 22 attempts.

"I thought Collin was amazing. We put the ball in his hands a lot, (and he) put a lot of pressure on them. Again, Ole Miss deserves all the credit, they made the plays, but it felt like we were not playing intelligent," Young said.

"... It was just frustrating because we felt like it was self-inflicted wounds ... for me, the biggest takeaway is just having better offensive integrity coming into a game where we know a team's going to be super aggressive (defensively)."

With Tuesday's performance, Ole Miss is KenPom's No. 1-rated defensive unit, boasting an adjusted efficiency mark of 89.6 — more than a point better than No. 2 Houston.

As for BYU's perimeter operation, the Cougars are now 11 for 51 (22%) from 3-point range in Maui, after having shot 42% from deep back in Utah.

So much for those famous "soft rims" at the Lahaina Civic Center.

"I thought this was a game where we would get a lot of open looks. If you look at the starters, by way of example, I mean, Collin goes 3 of 6, and then you've got Jax (Kohler) Bruce, Tyler (Betsey), Jake (Wahlin), that lineup went 0 for 18. It's going to be tough to win games when that happens," Young said.

"We have a lot of good shooting. All of our guys know that they can make shots, and I look forward to seeing more of that tomorrow, where they're actually going in."

With the loss, BYU is now 6-1 on the season and eliminated from Maui Invitational championship contention, as the 1992-93 Cougars will remain the only team in school history to reach the event's title game.

BYU will face either Arizona or Providence in Wednesday's third-place game at 3:30 p.m. MST.

"You just flush (today) and you move on. We've got to worry about what type of binds whoever we are going to play is going to put us in," Young said.

"Then, once we get home from this tournament, then you kind of do a deep dive on what you learned from the tournament as a whole."

articles.title: Does it matter how star-studded Sixers are winning and losing games?
articles.summary: One has to wonder if it matters how the star-studded Philadelphia 76ers are winning and losing games.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers are sitting at 14-4 and atop the Eastern Conference despite Monday's 128-111 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers at home. The Sixers are 12-0 in clutch games (games categorized as a 5-point spread or less with five minutes left in the game) and they have been terrific in terms of closing games out, but one has to wonder if it matters how the Sixers are winning and losing games.

Of their 14 wins, four of them have been by double-figures, and all four of their losses have been by double-figures. Therefore, one can summarize that the Sixers are winning close games, but losing in a tough fashion in those instances.

By true logic, a win is a win, and that's all that matters in the grand scheme of things, but to some, it does matter how the Sixers are winning.

"Yes. It matters because we want to build habits," said LeBron James after the win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Nov. 21. "We want to try to take steps forward every game that we get the opportunity to do. I know sometimes that it doesn't happen that way, but we want to do that. We want to strive to be as great as we can every night, offensively, defensively, special teams. So, yeah, I mean, a win is a win, but there is ways to win, and there's ways to continue to build habits throughout the course of this marathon."

Building wining habits is the name of the game right now. The Sixers can lean on their talent of James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, VJ Edgecombe, and others, but that won't matter unless they have the correct habits. Philadelphia has gotten off to a good start as it has begun to rely on each other and trust each other, but there is work to be done.

"I think we've bought into the pass," James explained. "We have so many guys that can score the ball at elite levels, and we know how we all, myself, VJ, JB, Max, Anfernee (Simons). You know, we have guys that can beat guys off the bounce. We know we have that in our ability. But in order for us to be like a super complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious, and it also just, it's key for our other guys as well to make sure to they feel like in a rhythm and they feel confident."

There were times it felt like the Sixers were doing a bit too much in terms of trying to get everybody going with the passing, but James sees improvements. There are still areas Philadelphia needs to get better in, like the defensive end of the floor as there has been slippage in recent games, but the Sixers are in a good spot.

"I think early on, like preseason, it looked a little weird," James continued. "Guys were like overpassing, you know, looking weird. But that's been great. And I think for the majority, our defense has been really good for the majority of the season. Tonight wasn't so great, but we've been really good defensively throughout the course of the season. Actually, better than our offense if you look at the numbers and things like that. So I don't want to say anything bad. There's so many things for us to do better, for sure."

So, does it matter how the Sixers win and lose games? Maybe so, but Philadelphia is succeeding in a lot of areas and it is winning basketball games. There is still work to be done, but the goal isn't to peak in November. The goal is to peak in April and May.

"There's games where we can defensive rebound a lot better," James finished. "There's games we can not turn the ball over. There's games where we can be a little bit more physically, physical defensively at the point of attack, like tonight. Wouldn't say anything has been bad, though, and that's a good thing. We want to continue to have room for improvement, and we don't want to be great in November either. That will be weird."

articles.title: What Ole Miss basketball’s Chris Beard said about Rebels’ insane comeback win over BYU
articles.summary: As the Ole Miss basketball team added another win to their season to put them at 6-0, it wasn’t just any ordinary victory, with the program getting a 73-63 r...
articles.body:
As the Ole Miss basketball team added another win to their season to put them at 6-0, it wasn't just any ordinary victory, with the program getting a 73-63 result against the No. 19 BYU Cougars. With the Ole Miss basketball team led by head coach Chris Beard , he would give his thoughts on the win, but more importantly, how the Rebels executed a marvelous comeback.

In the Southwest Maui Invitational game on Tuesday, the unranked Rebels were down to the Cougars at halftime, 40-26, but a spark was made in the second half by Ole Miss. With the Rebels outscoring the Cougars in the second half, 47-23, Beard was asked by Andy Katz what went into the halftime adjustments, giving insight into what the locker room was like.

"We have a veteran team," Beard said. "These guys have worked really hard since the first day of the summer. We've had some adversity along the way. This was our first adversity in the regular season, but it was really a calm halftime, and just asking the guys like, 'Hey, man, we're in the Maui Invitational. Are we going to compete this half?' Then once we decided we were going to play a little bit harder, then we got back to the original game plan."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Chris Beard continues on Ole Miss basketball's comeback win over BYU

The Ole Miss basketball team has been on a roll this season, but the win over BYU could give them national attention, especially when it comes to the rankings. Beard said that the comeback win over the Cougars is one that he will "remember."

"A tale of both halves," Beard continued. "Give BYU a lot of credit playing under man without their playmakers, but give our guys a lot of credit too. We're here. We came to Maui to win three games. Most people maybe didn't think that was probable, but we have an opportunity tomorrow to do that."

At any rate, Beard and the Rebels look to keep it going with their next game on Wednesday afternoon in the invitational, though the opponent has yet to be determined.

articles.title: Lakers are 15-3, but here’s why 1 ESPN insider is hating on NBA title contender status
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are having a blast to start the 2026-27 NBA season, but not everyone is completely sold just yet on the team’s status as an NBA champi...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are having a blast to start the 2026-27 NBA season, but not everyone is completely sold just yet on the team's status as an NBA championship contender.

Luka Doncic and the Lakers have a 15-3 record entering Tuesday, tied for the best record (but technically second) with the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference standings. They have also lost just once over their last 10 outings. For Tim MacMahon of ESPN, however, that record is not enough to label the Lakers as a legitimate NBA title contender, simply because he has yet to see the team take on some of the better teams in the league.

"I think the biggest overreaction is that the Lakers are clearly championship contenders," MacMahon said on Get Up YouTube Exclusive. "I'm not saying they can't be. I'm just saying they haven't proven to be with this great start that they've had against the No. 29 schedule in terms of opponents' winning percentage."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

For what it's worth, the Lakers are in the bottom five of the league through Monday in terms of in-season strength of schedule, according to Dunks and Threes. But MacMahon and other Lakers doubters can find out more about LA's true strength when the team hits th road for an upcoming road trip. That includes an upcoming Lakers-Spurs showdown on Friday.

"Now we're gonna learn a lot more about the Lakers over these next few games," MacMahon continued. "They've got a road trip at San Antonio, at Memphis, at Houston. You know, if they come out of that road trip looking rosy, then maybe it's time to reconsider. But I think it's premature to put the Lakers in the conversation with the best teams in the league."

articles.title: Joyce Edwards out for No. 1 South Carolina's clash with No. 7 UConn
articles.summary: The junior forward leads the 6-0 Gamecocks in scoring at 18 points per game.
articles.body:
No. 1 South Carolina will be without its top scorer for Tuesday's clash with No. 7 UConn . The Gamecocks announced approximately an hour before tip-off that Joyce Edwards is out of the lineup due to illness.

Edwards is South Carolina's leading scorer at 18 points per game, while also averaging 6.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.8 steals. She has started the Gamecocks' past 46 games.

This story will be updated with more information.

articles.title: South Carolina's Joyce Edwards out against UConn
articles.summary: Joyce Edwards will miss Tuesday's game for South Carolina because of illness. The No. 1-ranked Gamecocks face No. 8 UConn.
articles.body:
The No. 1-ranked South Carolina women's basketball team will be without Joyce Edwards for their matchup against No. 8 UConn at Mohegan Sun Arena on Tuesday, Nov. 24.

The junior forward is out for the game due to illness, the team announced via social media.

Edwards is the Gamecocks' leading scorer this season, averaging 18 points per game. A five-star recruit out of Camden High School, Edwards has spent her entire collegiate career under South Carolina coach Dawn Staley.

Edwards took over with 22 points in 18 minutes in South Carolina's last game, a 73-43 win over Providence on Saturday, Nov. 21. Freshman forward Oliviyah Edwards missed that game because she was also under the weather, but appears to be available for Tuesday's game.

Without Edwards, senior guard Tessa Johnson will be tasked with more scoring pressure against the Huskies. Johnson is averaging 15.7 points and 3.7 rebounds per game.

articles.title: Pistons announce oblique injury update for rookie Ebuka Okorie
articles.summary: Pistons rookie guard Ebuka Okorie will be sidelined with an injury suffered while on assignment last week in the G League.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons rookie guard Ebuka Okorie will be sidelined with an injury suffered while on assignment in the G League, the team announced on Tuesday.

Okorie sustained a left oblique strain early in the first quarter on Nov. 17 with the Motor City Cruise while driving to the rim against the Grand Rapids Gold. He was ruled out of returning to the game, finishing scoreless in 4 minutes, 4 seconds.

The medical staff will reevaluate the 17th overall pick in two weeks, sidelining him for at least five games. The team will provide further injury updates for Okorie as appropriate.

Okorie has played sparingly for the Pistons early on, averaging 2.2 points in four minutes per game across five appearances. He has been out of the rotation for coach J.B. Bickerstaff, which led to his assignment with the Cruise.

The 6-foot-2 Okorie was highly touted out of Stanford for his ability to pull up from virtually anywhere and put tremendous pressure on defenses, averaging 7.3 free-throw attempts per game. He also registered eight 30-point performances, the most by a freshman in ACC history.

Okorie earned praise from Bickerstaff in training camp for his demeanor, poise and finishing. While he hasn't had the chance to play much yet on a veteran-laden roster, he and the team hope he misses minimal time.
